newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares up as investors sense stability.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares up as investors sense stability.

text.p: Slovenian shares inched higher on Thursday, buoyed by optimism over the country's political future, and traders predicted the positive mood would make for further gains over the next few days.
"Investors have returned, mostly buying shares in companies like Lek, Droga and SKB banka, and that has pulled the market up," said Milos Obed, a trader at bank "A".

The 10-share SBI index rose 3.76 points to 1,183.7, building on Wednesday's 1.1 percent gain. Turnover fell to 176.7 million tolars from 258.3 million. Overall 15 shares rose, one fell and one was unchanged, eight were untraded.

Hopes for a speedy formation of Slovenia's new government were fed earlier this week when parliament almost unanimously voted for Janez Podobnik of the People's Party, part of the rightist "Spring alliance" that wants to oust Liberal Democrat Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek, as the assembly's new president.

The move, which came three weeks after a general election that gave neither right nor left a clear mandate to run the country, was widely seen as hinting the two sides had reached an agreement that would allow Drnovsek to remain in power.
Drug maker Lek A issue the most actively traded share for the second day in a row, firming 1.01 percent to 19,950 tolars on volume of 2,055 shares.
Brokerage Dadas was the biggest gainer, rising 6.31 percent to 12,130 tolars on volume of 832 shares.
Food maker Kolinska was the day's only decliner, easing 0.20 percent to 1,991 tolars on volume of 4,522 tolars.
Food producer Droga rose 0.93 percent to 21,800 tolars on volume of 128 shares.
Bank SKB, which last month announced plans for a foreign listing next year, rose 0.59 percent to 42,290 tolars on volume of 453 shares.
